review_type: Repository-owner-commissioned AI-assisted Econometrica numerical-methods advisory review
recommendation: Reject in the present form and do not invite another ordinary revision of the cumulative manuscript. A new, sharply focused paper on acquisition-aware, witness-preserving Bellman certification for constrained Lipschitz dynamic programs could merit evaluation after the contribution is isolated, the publication object is made canonical, and direct constrained-policy and total-work comparisons are supplied.

publication_status.first_failure: All 69 tests and three LaTeX passes completed; publication audit stopped because pdfinfo was unavailable.

blocking_findings: R47 is not a canonical completed submitted manuscript: the intended review-ready branch is absent and the latest publication workflow did not complete.
The central witness backend is a classical min-plus/Lipschitz-envelope algorithm whose native and ReLU representations are mathematically identical; no neural computational advantage is identified.
All 120 direct scalar policy-cost intervals contain zero; the result establishes only proximity inside an uncalibrated normalized tolerance band.
The constrained witness has a 13.3-17.2 percent tighter bound but is roughly 21 times slower than bilinear FVI, and neither method attains the tighter targets.
No direct expected-policy-cost comparison is supplied for the new constrained witness and bilinear-FVI policies.
The scalar frontier compares prefix Bellman-query counts rather than complete method-inclusive work.
The nonlinear construction remains two-dimensional and tensor-cover dependent, with O(TN^6) direct cone work versus O(TN^4) bilinear work.
Acquisition error can add approximately 0.36 to the uniform policy bound at the coarsest executed radius, without an economically calibrated sensor model.
The finite catalogue and identical deterministic repetitions do not establish optimizer population reliability or hardware-general performance.
The broad cumulative platform framing and economic claims remain disproportionate to the narrow certification result and normalized examples.
positive_findings: The direct policy-cost difference is now the estimand rather than a subtraction of separate regret bounds.
The acquisition-aware theorem handles discontinuous witness selection through objective and feasibility allowances rather than actor continuity.
State-dependent capacity repair and continuous-law integration are explicitly constructed and executed in a two-state nonlinear economy.
The native min-plus and ReLU representations are explicitly identified as one construction rather than counted as independent methods.
The complete frozen scalar certificate frontier includes favorable, adverse, tied and unattained intervals.
All adverse timing, target-attainment, ambiguity, repair and publication outcomes are retained.
Source freezing, record hashes, preservation and artifact provenance are unusually strong.

limitations: The reviewer did not rerun training, simulation, LaTeX or timing services; new executions would create new observations.
The review verifies frozen records, hashes and aggregate arithmetic and spot-checks the main theorem chain; it is not an independent proof of every inherited result.
Single-host timings are descriptive and support no hardware-general inference.
No claim is made that bilinear FVI dominates outside the declared constrained economies.
This advisory review is not an Econometric Society editorial decision.
